entries.opening: Building a cart behind closed doors and having it fit the ruts outside names a claim that private construction can meet the public road exactly.
entries.zenBend: Masters turn the proverb into a public challenge: Daqianshan asks what “building the cart” is, while Xuedou says merely claiming the fit is cave-work.
entries.scopeLimit: The corpus contests and tests the claimed fit; the dictionary does not decide that every private construction succeeds.

entries.opening: Adding frost on top of snow is adding a needless complication to something already complete or already difficult.
entries.zenBend: Masters apply it to extra words, extra judgments, and explanations that compound rather than settle the case.
entries.scopeLimit: The phrase can criticize an addition without defining every cited teaching as mistaken.

entries.opening: Adding flowers on top of brocade is an additional embellishment placed on something already splendid or complete.
entries.zenBend: Zen records use it for a further answer, verse, or action that adorns an already sufficient presentation, sometimes approvingly and sometimes with an edge.
entries.scopeLimit: The stored uses do not make every addition either praise or blame; the surrounding verdict controls the tone.

entries.opening: Putting grit in the eye is introducing an obstruction precisely where clear seeing is at stake.
entries.zenBend: Masters use it against added formulations, names, and even revered claims when those additions interfere with the immediate exchange.
entries.scopeLimit: It is a contextual rebuke to an addition, not a claim that words or names are always obstructive.

entries.opening: Gouging a sore into sound flesh is creating a problem or complication where none was required.
entries.zenBend: Masters apply the image to surplus explanation, forced distinctions, and their own unavoidable speech before an assembly.
entries.scopeLimit: The phrase criticizes the added wound while allowing speakers to acknowledge that their own explanation is such an addition.
